New edema and enhancement in the L6 spinous process. Collectively findings concerning for progression of discitis-osteomyelitis.   2. New edema and enhancement in the right L5 to L6 and left L6-S1 facet joints, which could represent septic arthritis.  3. Interval enlargement of dorsal epidural abscess from L4 to S1. Interval enlargement in small abscesses adjacent to the left L6-S1 facet joint.   4. Severe central canal narrowing at L5-L6, L6-S1 secondary to degenerative changes and the dorsal epidural abscess.  This is a preliminary report dictated by Dr. Alice Shieh PGY-4.  Unless an Attending Final Impression appears below, the report has not yet been finalized and an attending radiologist has not reviewed these images.    ATTENDING FINAL REPORT  I agree with the preliminary report with the following comment(s).  Cervical spine: Interval decrease in size of C2 ventral epidural phlegmon/abscess with minimal residual collection measuring up to approximately 5 mm in greatest width. Worsening enhancement within the paraspinal soft tissues extending into the interspinous ligaments from C1-C2 to C3-C4 with new serpiginous, rim-enhancing fluid collection measuring roughly 1.8 x 0.6 x 2.2 cm centered within the paraspinal soft tissues along the C2 spinous process (series 21 image 11 and series 20 image 9) most concerning for interval development of a small abscess. Enhancement now extends adjacent to the left-sided C2-C3 articular facet which may represent additional site of septic arthritis. Posterior disc osteophyte complex at C3-C4 which results in moderate spinal canal stenosis with indentation of the right ventral cord.  Thoracic spine: As above.  Lumbar spine:  Spine numbering as above.  Interval bilateral laminotomies at the level labeled L5-L6 and L6-S1 (previously labeled as L4-L5 and L5-S1). The prior dorsal epidural abscess at this level has resolved. Increased enhancement within the paraspinal soft tissues extending along the bilateral facet joints which may be postoperative with the possibility of superimposed infection/septic arthritis not excluded by imaging.   There is, however, persistent enhancement within the L5 and L6 vertebral bodies/spinous processes with increased enhancement extending into the intervertebral disc space, worsening disc height loss as well as extension of enhancement into the prevertebral soft tissues. Appearance is concerning for progression of discitis/osteomyelitis. Additionally, there is a new ventral left paracentral rim-enhancing collection measuring up to approximately 2.8 cm in greatest craniocaudal dimension (series 24 image 80) extending from the L5-L6 level to S1. This results in moderate L6-S1 spinal canal stenosis with severe narrowing of the left subarticular recess and left-sided neural foramen resulting in compression upon the exiting and transversing left-sided nerve roots. Appearance is most concerning for interval development of a new ventral epidural abscess. Clumping/peripheral displacement of the cauda equina nerve roots compatible with arachnoiditis. Near complete resolution of the previously noted prevertebral abscess from T9 to T11, without discrete measurable fluid collection. Residual prevertebral soft tissue thickening and enhancement.  Lumbar spine:  1. Increased edema and enhancement of the L5 to L6 disc space. Edema and enhancement of the adjacent L5 to L6 endplates is minimally decreased from prior. New edema and enhancement in the L6 spinous process. Collectively findings concerning for progression of discitis-osteomyelitis.   2. New edema and enhancement in the right L5 to L6 and left L6-S1 facet joints, which could represent septic arthritis.  3. Interval enlargement of dorsal epidural abscess from L4 to S1. Interval enlargement in small abscesses adjacent to the left L6-S1 facet joint.   4. Severe central canal narrowing at L5-L6, L6-S1 secondary to degenerative changes and the dorsal epidural abscess.  This is a preliminary report dictated by Dr. Alice Shieh PGY-4.  Unless an Attending Final Impression appears below, the report has not yet been finalized and an attending radiologist has not reviewed these images.    ATTENDING FINAL REPORT  I agree with the preliminary report with the following comment(s).  Cervical spine: Interval decrease in size of C2 ventral epidural phlegmon/abscess with minimal residual collection measuring up to approximately 5 mm in greatest width. Worsening enhancement within the paraspinal soft tissues extending into the interspinous ligaments from C1-C2 to C3-C4 with new serpiginous, rim-enhancing fluid collection measuring roughly 1.8 x 0.6 x 2.2 cm centered within the paraspinal soft tissues along the C2 spinous process (series 21 image 11 and series 20 image 9) most concerning for interval development of a small abscess. Enhancement now extends adjacent to the left-sided C2-C3 articular facet which may represent additional site of septic arthritis. Posterior disc osteophyte complex at C3-C4 which results in moderate spinal canal stenosis with indentation of the right ventral cord.  Thoracic spine: As above.  Lumbar spine:  Spine numbering as above.  Interval bilateral laminotomies at the level labeled L5-L6 and L6-S1 (previously labeled as L4-L5 and L5-S1). The prior dorsal epidural abscess at this level has resolved. Increased enhancement within the paraspinal soft tissues extending along the bilateral facet joints which may be postoperative with the possibility of superimposed infection/septic arthritis not excluded by imaging.   There is, however, persistent enhancement within the L5 and L6 vertebral bodies/spinous processes with increased enhancement extending into the intervertebral disc space, worsening disc height loss as well as extension of enhancement into the prevertebral soft tissues. Appearance is concerning for progression of discitis/osteomyelitis. Additionally, there is a new ventral left paracentral rim-enhancing collection measuring up to approximately 2.8 cm in greatest craniocaudal dimension (series 24 image 80) extending from the L5-L6 level to S1. This results in moderate L6-S1 spinal canal stenosis with severe narrowing of the left subarticular recess and left-sided neural foramen resulting in compression upon the exiting and transversing left-sided nerve roots. Appearance is most concerning for interval development of a new ventral epidural abscess. Clumping/peripheral displacement of the cauda equina nerve roots compatible with arachnoiditis. ATTENDING FINAL REVIEW  Addendum to the preliminary report.  -At L4-L5 level, there appears to be diffuse irregularity of the articular surfaces of bilateral facet joints, right greater than left, with associated surrounding soft tissue edema and enhancement, with adjacent small rim-enhancing left dorsal epidural fluid collection which demonstrates restricted diffusion on DWI. The collection measures approximately 5 mm in greatest dimension (series 2001 image 31). Also seen is ill-defined soft tissue enhancement surrounding L2-L3 facet joints, with extensive paraspinal muscle edema and enhancement in the lumbar spine. Extensive signal alteration and degenerative changes with associated enhancement centered about the L4-5 disc space and facet joints, with imaging features suggestive of neuropathic (Charcot) arthropathy. 4ce1d8d16b83cb28e2b9ed86202d9b3172289332.text: 1.  Focal heterogenously enhancing intramedullary lesion at T3-T4 is associated with extensive cord edema but no significant mass effect or cord swelling. No prior MRI's are available for direct comparison.  Given the finding of radiation-induced marrow signal changes from T1 to T5 vertebral body, this cord lesion is favored to represent treatment effects/radiation necrosis. Metastatic renal cell carcinoma to the cord has been described in the literature, but is exceedingly rare and is considered less likely, although the possibility of a previously treated, recurrent cord metastasis cannot be entirely excluded. If there is clinical concern for an acute traumatic injury in the cervical spine, correlation with CT is advised, as acute fractures can be occult on MRI. ATTENDING FINAL REPORT  FINDINGS/IMPRESSION (final): I agree with the preliminary report with the following comment(s):  Nonspecific diffuse marrow signal alteration within the visualized vertebral bodies, most notably involving the L5 vertebral body, with associated diffuse heterogeneous enhancement concerning for possible nonspecific infiltrative process including neoplastic involvement. Similar heterogeneous enhancement identified within the visualized sacrum (S1-S3), for which osseous neoplastic involvement be difficult to entirely exclude. Patchy enhancing lesions within the bilateral iliac crests, left greater than right, concerning for osseous metastases.  There is diffuse, thickened enhancement throughout the retroperitoneum, surrounding the bilateral kidneys, paraspinal musculature including the iliopsoas muscles, and extending into the bilateral neural foramina of the visualized S1, L5, L4, L3, and to a lesser extent L2 and possibly L1 vertebral levels. While the appearance is nonspecific and could be attributed to venous engorgement, given extent of known, diffuse intra-abdominal neoplastic involvement, findings are concerning for diffuse neoplastic foraminal infiltration including extension to the epidural space (most notably at the lumbosacral junction (see image 40 of series 8). The extent of mass effect upon specific exiting nerve roots is difficult to assess but maybe moderate to severe at L5-S1, and to a lesser extent at L4-5. No definite intrathecal enhancement identified. However, correlation with lumbar puncture and histologic sampling may be of benefit.  Redemonstration of numerous intrahepatic lesions, which are partially cystic, incompletely evaluated on the current examination. There is marked prominence of the midportion of the common bile duct and main pancreatic duct, as described in report for associated same day CT abdomen pelvis. Query nonspecific left adrenal mass (image 11 of series 5), measuring personally 1.6 cm in diameter. Diffuse ascites.  I have personally reviewed the images and agree with the report (or as edited).

Diffuse enhancement of C2 and anterior C1, with a loculated prevertebral abscess, epidural infection extending ventrally to C2-C3 and dorsally to approximately mid C5. Leptomeningeal enhancement of the ventral surface of the brainstem. Severe compression of the spinal cord at the foramen magnum, with T2 hyperintensity extending from mid C2 into the medulla. Enhancement extends into the C2-C3 3 foramina bilaterally, with narrowing of both vertebral arteries and possible abrupt occlusion of the left vertebral artery (9/5-6). There is 11 mm of basilar invagination of the tip of the dens through the foramen magnum.  MRI of the head may be helpful to further delineate the superior aspect of the infection. Incidental note is made of diminutive kidneys bilaterally, both with cystic lesions. A presumed renal transplant is incompletely imaged within the right hemipelvis.  I have personally reviewed the images and agree with the report (or as edited).
